title: OpenAI employee arrested and charged over hidden recording
content:
Federal authorities arrested a Saudi national employed at OpenAI and charged him with planting a recording device in a company’s executive conference room, the Department of Justice announced Tuesday.

On or around Sept. 30, OpenAI discovered a sophisticated recording device inserted into the back of a television in an executive conference room located in one of its San Francisco offices. The company determined that the device was installed approximately a couple days prior, concealed in toilet paper. The contents of the device were encrypted, according to the DOJ.

The Department of Justice said in a news release that the employee, Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, was arrested Friday and appeared in federal court Tuesday. OpenAI confirmed the incident on social media and said that it was supporting the FBI’s investigation.

“We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier,” OpenAI said in its statement. “At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data.”
snippet: Federal authorities arrested a Saudi national employed at OpenAI and charged him with planting a recording device in a company’s executive conference room, the Department of Justice announced Tuesday.
creator: Ashley Ahn

title: Europe’s leaders abandon the race for frontier AI
content:
BRUSSELS — As the U.S. and China compete to train the world’s most advanced artificial intelligence models, Europe is stepping back.

European politicians and tech executives have in recent weeks shifted their focus away from frontier AI as it becomes clear the bloc has no artificial intelligence models that can compete with top American or Chinese models, and Europe’s leading contender Mistral faces questions over its performance.

Instead, a new mantra has emerged: Europe doesn’t need to own the models as long as it can put them to work.

“Striving to build a competitive frontier lab right now feels like very wishful thinking,” said Max Junestrand, CEO of Swedish AI company Legora, a €6 billion company that provides an AI tool for law firms. “I would rather see us put more thinking cycles into how do we capitalize on the technology rather than how do we try to catch up.”

The suggestion that frontier AI models are now out of reach for European AI labs comes as the most advanced models become a major global security issue.
snippet: BRUSSELS — As the U.S. and China compete to train the world’s most advanced artificial intelligence models, Europe is stepping back.
creator: Pieter Haeck

title: How Maroš Šefčovič talked his way to a China trade breakthrough
content:
Europe’s trade chief has won a first concession from Beijing. Now he must convince EU leaders that dialogue can deliver more.

By Camille Gijs and Carlo Martuscelli
in Brussels

Illustration by Natália Delgado/POLITICO

When Maroš Šefčovič set out his strategy for engaging with China to European Union ambassadors in July, he had a warning for governments urging tougher action on trade against Beijing.

“Sometimes, it’s even popular to start a trade war, but it’s very difficult to finish it,” the EU trade chief recalled later in an interview with POLITICO.

Three months on, Šefčovič has secured a first breakthrough, reaching a deal in Beijing last week to sharply reduce imports of Chinese hybrid cars. The symbolic win marks a small step toward stabilizing a trading relationship that Brussels believes has reached a dangerous tipping point.

The agreement, which will initially cap imports at 350,000 vehicles a year, marks a significant concession from Beijing, whose carmakers have been flooding the European market with increasingly competitive vehicles.

Europe’s trade chief has won a first concession from Beijing. Now he must convince EU leaders that dialogue can deliver more.

title: Lights, bells and liability: Europe’s privacy regulators crack down on smart glasses
content:
BRUSSELS — Privacy regulators want people wearing smart glasses in public to look and sound like a truck backing down a road.

Europe’s powerful data regulators have made stringent new recommendations on how smart glasses should alert people that the wearable devices are filming, including a combination of flashing lights, audio alerts and notifications sent to the phones of people nearby.

The European Data Protection Board (EDPB), made up of national privacy regulators across Europe, issued a statement about smart glasses on Tuesday, following a meeting in Brussels.

Privacy regulators are putting forward a united front on smart glasses, as privacy concerns about the wearable technology have multiplied since videos made with them have begun spreading online without the knowledge or consent of those being filmed.

The statement is not legally binding but will guide how privacy regulators in Europe assess whether smart glasses users and manufacturers are complying with EU privacy rules like the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
snippet: BRUSSELS — Privacy regulators want people wearing smart glasses in public to look and sound like a truck backing down a road.
creator: Ellen O'Regan

title: MI5 to step up on AI threats amid bioweapon risk
content:
LONDON — Britain’s spies will have a leading role in Britain’s preparation for AI threats, the head of MI5 announced on Tuesday, after warning the technology could enable terrorists to access bioweapons.

Ken McCallum, director general of the U.K.’s domestic intelligence agency has established the AI Threat Assessment Centre to help determine how the government views potential threats.

Giving his annual threat update from MI5 headquarters in London, McCallum said: “Human history has given us no experience of facing an actor which is smarter than we are, is capable of outthinking us.”

He stressed the “real” risks of AI, saying MI5 has caught terrorists seeking to use AI to “improve their reconnaissance and attack methodologies,” in addition to the danger of AI-enabled drones.

Though it has not yet been “realized,” he said he attaches “the greatest weight” to AI’s potential to “change the stakes on existing or even new bioweapons.”

He said “low-capability” terrorists may get a “capability” uplift if the safety guardrails in AI models don’t work as intended.

title: France’s Philippe says Le Pen’s EU proposals would ‘crack open’ bloc
content:
PARIS — French center-right presidential candidate Edouard Philippe accused his far-right rival Marine Le Pen of trying to force a Frexit in disguise with her euroskeptic campaign promises.

“There is something in Marine Le Pen’s proposals that has the potential to blow Europe up, or let’s say to crack it open,” Philippe said at POLITICO’s Paris Competitiveness Summit on Tuesday.

The former prime minister — who is currently the best-placed centrist candidate to challenge the front-running Le Pen, according to recent polls — said Le Pen’s plan to unilaterally demand a drastic cut to France’s contribution to the EU budget was akin to “saying you want out of Europe” without openly advocating for leaving the bloc. Le Pen had previously called for a referendum in France on leaving the EU but dropped the proposal after her crushing defeat to Emmanuel Macron in the 2017 presidential election. Her party, the National Rally, now says it wants to change the EU from within.
snippet: PARIS — French center-right presidential candidate Edouard Philippe accused his far-right rival Marine Le Pen of trying to force a Frexit in disguise with her euroskeptic campaign promises.
creator: Marion Solletty, Pauline de Saint Remy

title: Document: Germany, Italy request ‘emergency brake’ power to stop new EU laws
content:
EU capitals must be able to intervene to stop new legislation from Brussels if they say it’s too burdensome for governments and businesses, the leaders of Germany, Italy and Belgium wrote on Monday.

In a letter addressed to European Council President António Costa and obtained by POLITICO, the three leaders said the bloc needs an “emergency brake” mechanism to help boost its flagging economic competitiveness.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Belgian Prime Minister Bart de Wever also called to “significantly accelerate planning and approval procedures,” suspend “certain regulatory areas for a specified period” under a new “priority rule.”

“We call for further ambitious simplification packages to decisively advance the cutting of red tape in the European Union,” they wrote, adding that the Commission must ease the burden “first and foremost” on small and medium-sized businesses.

“More broadly,” the letter reads, “our common objective should be to prevent unnecessary regulatory burdens and related costs from causing permanent losses of European industrial capacity and further weakening investment and competitiveness.”
snippet: EU capitals must be able to intervene to stop new legislation from Brussels if they say it’s too burdensome for governments and businesses, the leaders of Germany, Italy and Belgium wrote on Monday.
creator: Nicholas Vinocur, Anouk Schlung

title: Von der Leyen pitches AI as solution to reduce reporting for European businesses
content:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Monday pitched using artificial intelligence to streamline administrative procedures for European businesses as part of a broader push to simplify commerce and boost the EU’s competitiveness.

Speaking at a behind-closed-doors meeting of the European People’s Party in Taormina, Sicily, on Oct. 12, von der Leyen said the Commission would introduce an “only once” approach to business reporting. This would let companies submit information once, with AI helping public administrations use the data.

Von der Leyen argued that European companies repeatedly have to report the same information to public authorities, wasting time that businesses — and Europe — cannot afford, according to a copy of her speech seen by POLITICO.

“And this is why we will introduce ‘Only Once’, to report data only once – and with the help of AI the administration will ensure efficient use,” she said.

The speech marks the first time von der Leyen has explicitly pitched using AI specifically to reduce businesses’ administrative workload.

title: How Europe plans to squeeze out Starlink
content:
BRUSSELS — Stepping on stage at the International Space Summit in Paris, French President Emmanuel Macron called on top European players to forge a new “alliance” to strengthen collective satellite capacity.

The real target of the let’s-team-up message? Elon Musk’s Starlink.

Macron’s speech last month was a public endorsement of a behind-the-scenes push that would see the bloc’s major telecoms companies make an aggressive play on direct-to-device connectivity — mobile signals beamed directly from satellites to phones.

On Tuesday, telecom ministers from EU national governments are gathering in Limerick, Ireland, to discuss a legislative proposal that could make it easier for top European carriers to get that satellite access.

The push would see Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Vodafone and Telefónica join forces to secure critical and coveted frequencies that will become available next year, as the European Commission eyes a new allocation procedure that would reserve frequencies for European players.

The plan, reported by Bloomberg ahead of Macron’s Sept. 10 speech, was confirmed to POLITICO by two people aware of the talks.

title: How can Europe leverage laws to secure cloud sovereignty?
content:
European organizations have to reckon with how to keep up with the modern world without sacrificing sovereignty. Geopolitical instability, tightening regulatory expectations and the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) mean that, for many organizations, sovereignty now sits alongside resilience and business continuity in board-level risk discussions. The question they can no longer defer is how to harness the opportunities of the modern cloud without surrendering control over their own data. Answering it requires honesty about what sovereignty means, and about where it can actually be found.

title: Turkey bans social media for kids under 15
content:
The government of Turkey on Saturday formally banned access to social media platform for children under the age of 15.

The law was published today following the Turkish Parliament’s adoption of the bill last April. The ban will come into force on Nov. 1.

Social media platforms will have to “take the necessary technical and administrative measures, including age verification,” to implement the new rules, the law states. The age verification system would work with a government-issued “token”, according to the law’s Article 7.

The law also includes provisions for minors over 15, stating that platforms cannot offer them services that could have “an addictive effect.”

Turkey has often implemented tough restrictions on social media services, frequently banning individual accounts from media outlets or activists, and at times banning access to entire platforms. Ankara banned Instagram for a week in 2024 amid claims the Meta-owned platform censored users mourning Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh.

Last week Turkey blocked a news website and its social media accounts over what a court deemed to be “LGBT propaganda,” sparking outrage from human rights and media freedom groups.
snippet: The government of Turkey on Saturday formally banned access to social media platform for children under the age of 15.
creator: Marianne Gros

title: EU cyber and science researchers are testing Chinese AI models
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Union’s cybersecurity agency and in-house research center have each begun experimenting with open artificial intelligence models from China, three EU officials have told POLITICO.

The Joint Research Centre (JRC) — the EU’s in-house scientific research center — is evaluating “publicly available open-weight models” originating from China, European Commission spokesperson Maciej Berestecki confirmed. The head of ENISA, the bloc’s agency responsible for cybersecurity, also said in an interview that his team was now testing Chinese AI.

The experiments with Chinese models at the JRC are part of a broader research project to evaluate artificial intelligence that also includes leading models from the United States and Europe, Berestecki said. “Models from different origins are included in a comparative scientific evaluation of their capabilities, performance, limitations and risks,” he said, adding that the JRC is also looking into their potential scientific applications.

title: EU, Canada and Lithuania pull out of disinformation conference after US pressure
content:
The Trump administration pressured diplomatic officials from the EU, Canada and Lithuania to pull out of an international conference on disinformation after organizers announced panels warning of the threat posed by American government officials and the country’s influence broadly, according to excerpts of a State Department cable seen by POLITICO.

The conference, titled #Disinfo2026, included sessions that described the U.S. as a “foreign information manipulation and interference” actor, or “FIMI,” which bothered the Trump administration, according to the cable. The conference is being held Wednesday and Thursday in Vilnius, the Lithuanian capital.

The State Department asked American embassies in several European countries and the EU to express Washington’s concerns and “assess” whether the governments involved in the conference agree with the U.S. being characterized as a FIMI actor, according to the cable.

title: Read the charter for the White House’s ‘Super Intelligence Force’
content:
The Trump administration has given its newly created “Super Intelligence Force” broad authority to determine how the tech industry and the federal government should address threats to national security and civil liberties posed by fast-evolving artificial intelligence technology, according to a charter obtained by POLITICO.

Three people familiar with discussions about the task force confirmed the document’s authenticity. The people were granted anonymity to share details that are not yet public.

The task force will identify “measures to improve the preparedness and response capability of both the government and the private sector to threats to the homeland and the American people,” the charter states. It will also produce a report on the risks of AI, focusing on “potential threats to civil liberties,” cybersecurity, standards for advanced models, and the impacts of possible overregulation.

The Wall Street Journal first reported on the details of the charter.

title: The EU shelved AI liability rules. Sam Altman has revived the debate.
content:
BRUSSELS — EU parliamentarians are digging in on calls to revive an artificial intelligence liability law after receiving support from an unexpected ally: OpenAI’s Sam Altman.

“If something goes wrong with our models during training, there’s gonna be some version of that we need to be responsible for,” Altman said in an exclusive interview with Decoded by POLITICO released Monday. “There’s gonna need to be a liability framework for companies.”

This spotlight on liability has given influential members of the European Parliament a told-you-so moment after the EU last year scrapped plans to legislate on responsibility and compensation for harms caused by AI makers and agents.

The proposal by the European Commission for an AI liability law was killed amid a deep effort in Brussels to deregulate and reduce the legislative burden on companies — with the Commission arguing at the time that the proposal had little chance of securing sufficient political support.

German conservative lawmaker Axel Voss, who led on the proposal for the European Parliament, wants Brussels to put liability back on the agenda in light of Altman’s comments.
snippet: BRUSSELS — EU parliamentarians are digging in on calls to revive an artificial intelligence liability law after receiving support from an unexpected ally: OpenAI’s Sam Altman.
creator: Mathieu Pollet

title: German search engine ditches Mistral, bets on Chinese open-source AI
content:
BERLIN — A Berlin-based search engine used by government services is dropping its French AI partner, Mistral, in favor of open-source models, including those from China, its CEO told POLITICO.

“We are disappointed with the quality of Mistral,” Ecosia founder and CEO Christian Kroll said in an interview, stating that the models from France’s flagship AI lab are now “a year behind” the competition.

Ecosia — a German web browser and search engine that has built its brand on support for climate action and independence from non-European tech — is used by institutions ranging from Germany’s federal environment ministry to the U.K.’s National Health Service.

In May, it replaced the American giant OpenAI with Mistral as its AI provider. But the company experienced recurring technical problems, including overloaded servers, Kroll said. “We were simply too large a customer for Mistral,” Kroll said
snippet: BERLIN — A Berlin-based search engine used by government services is dropping its French AI partner, Mistral, in favor of open-source models, including those from China, its CEO told POLITICO.
creator: Anouk Schlung, Larissa Kögl

title: Jailed Albanian mayor uses AI avatar to make deepfake speech
content:
TIRANA, Albania — Tirana Mayor Erion Veliaj has caused a stir with a video pledge of free school lunches for all the capital’s children. There’s one problem: Veliaj is currently in prison, and the blue-suited figure making the heartfelt announcement is AI-generated.

In an Instagram post on his official profile labeled as AI-generated, the video likeness of the 46-year-old appears in front of the Albanian and municipal flags, listing his achievements in office while reiterating his promise of free school lunches for the city’s kids. 

“I made another commitment that I will never forget: food in schools,” says the Veliaj clone. “I will keep this promise even from this cell where they have locked me up.”

Veliaj has been in prison in the coastal city of Durres since early 2025 amid investigations over allegations of corruption and financial crimes. He denies any wrongdoing. 

“My hostage situation has been going on for 20 months, and I can only greet you with artificial intelligence,” his avatar says. “I will continue to work even from the cell … I hug you with longing, you and your wonderful children.”

title: Europe’s AI policing plan stokes privacy concerns
content:
BRUSSELS — Senior EU officials warn that a sweeping new plan to arm the bloc’s police agency, Europol, for the AI era could threaten Europeans’ privacy.

As cybercriminals, terrorists and spies weaponize artificial intelligence for scams, extortion and cyberattacks, Brussels is betting on expanding Europol’s AI powers — the agency that has coordinated European police intelligence since 1998 — to help combat the risks.

“Europol is at a turning point,” said centrist European Parliament member Fabienne Keller, who serves on the justice and civil liberties committee. While “we need a stronger Europol, with the resources and capabilities to effectively support national law enforcement authorities,” Keller said. That “must go hand-in-hand with strong democratic oversight and robust safeguards for fundamental rights and data protection.”

Plans for a “transformative evolution” of the The Hague-based agency, announced this summer, would double its budget to €3 billion and give Europol a hands-on role in fighting new threats, with access to more data and advanced technology.
snippet: BRUSSELS — Senior EU officials warn that a sweeping new plan to arm the bloc’s police agency, Europol, for the AI era could threaten Europeans’ privacy.
creator: Ellen O'Regan, Antoaneta Roussi

title: 50 members of European Parliament targeted by deepfake porn, report says
content:
Fifty European Union lawmakers, including 46 women, have been the targets of deepfake pornography, according to new research released Monday.

The number of women targeted by deepfake pornography — when generative AI is used to create sexually explicit depictions of people, often without their consent — means roughly one in six female members of the European Parliament have been affected, the report by Agora Digitale Transformation, a Germany-based civil society group, said.

The European Union is banning AI-powered nudifier apps on Dec. 2, and is also investigating similar use of Grok on the social media platform X.

A cross-party group of 119 MEPs called for effective enforcement of the ban and prompt resolution of the investigation into Grok, in a Sept. 30 letter sent to Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, the head of the Council of the EU Antonio Costa, Parliament President Roberta Metsola, EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen and Commissioner Hadja Lalhbib. The signatories included leaders of the liberal Renew, the socialists, and The Left: Iratxe Garcia Pérez, Valérie Hayer, and Manon Aubry, respectively.
snippet: Fifty European Union lawmakers, including 46 women, have been the targets of deepfake pornography, according to new research released Monday.
creator: Eliza Gkritsi

title: Merz and Macron want the EU to hit back harder — and faster — against trade threats
content:
BERLIN — The European Commission needs the power to act much faster against trade threats, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron urged in a joint letter on Monday.

The leaders of the EU’s two most powerful and populous countries want Brussels to be able to act more quickly and decisively in a trade confrontation — while making it harder for EU capitals to block action.

The proposal seeks to strengthen the hand of Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič, who flies to Beijing on Thursday for the final round of talks in a four-month process where Brussels is seeking to rebalance the EU’s trading relationship with China.

Merz and Macron said the Commission should be empowered to restrict, or even completely cut off, imports from countries seen as creating “severe and systematic distortions” in the single market. In their letter and a joint position paper, they call for urgent action, saying the EU’s existing trade defense toolbox “does not suffice anymore.”

“Without delaying the full use of the existing set of instruments, we need a comprehensive framework to complement our toolbox with new legal instruments — in a lean and non-bureaucratic way,” they wrote.
snippet: BERLIN — The European Commission needs the power to act much faster against trade threats, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and French President Emmanuel Macron urged in a joint letter on Monday.
creator: Hans von der Burchard, Carlo Martuscelli, Giorgio Leali, Jordyn Dahl, Camille Gijs

title: Emmanuel Macron is most impressive world leader on AI, says Sam Altman
content:
OpenAI’s Sam Altman named French President Emmanuel Macron as the world leader who stands out for their approach to AI in an exclusive interview with Decoded by POLITICO.

“The person that came to mind as you were saying that is the French president,” Altman told Decoded co-author and POLITICO senior tech reporter Brendan Bordelon in response to being asked who has impressed him the most with their AI policy or plans for the technology.

“I think [Macron] is extremely thoughtful and has been for a long time about where this is going and what the shape of it needs to look like,” Altman said.

The recognition is notable because Macron has sought to use his leadership to push AI safety on the global stage, and because the French president is months away from leaving office.

After two terms as president, Macron is barred from running in the next election in April 2027. The far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who is leading in the polls, is advocating a policy of deregulation on AI, three senior party officials told POLITICO.
snippet: OpenAI’s Sam Altman named French President Emmanuel Macron as the world leader who stands out for their approach to AI in an exclusive interview with Decoded by POLITICO.

title: Banks vs bots: Agentic AI opens up new fear for finance industry
content:
Artificial intelligence could kill us all. It might cause a financial meltdown first.  

The financial services industry is frantically embracing the use of agentic AI — a virtual assistant that pursues its goals with autonomy, rather than being ordered to do something.

Yet experts warn that the use of agentic AI in finance could result in bank deposits being moved rapidly from one lender to another, independent bots prompting investors to channel funds to the same target all at once or shoppers losing money.

Even in the best case scenario, they fear liability for mistakes will be a minefield. Their worst-case scenario includes runs on banks, financial institutions being brought down — and even the next financial crash.

Agentic commerce could orchestrate $3 to $5 trillion in revenue by 2030, according to research by McKinsey, creating much-needed growth in major economies struggling with debt amid the aftermath of the pandemic, ongoing wars and higher interest rates.
snippet: Artificial intelligence could kill us all. It might cause a financial meltdown first.

title: Sam Altman to Decoded: ‘The world should accept some bad things happening’ for the benefits of AI
content:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said there remains a fundamental difference in worldview between his company and rival Anthropic on artificial intelligence regulation, arguing in an exclusive interview with Decoded by POLITICO that the technology’s benefits justify accepting some risks — and that AI should remain broadly accessible to the public.

“I think there’s a lot of daylight,” Altman told Decoded co-author and POLITICO senior tech reporter Brendan Bordelon. Asked specifically where he diverges from Anthropic and its CEO Dario Amodei, Altman said, “we believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency.”

Anthropic has long been viewed as the strongest proponent of AI regulations within the industry, a stance that until recently was at odds with the lighter-touch approach favored by OpenAI. But the policy differences between the two leading AI firms have narrowed in recent months, with OpenAI backing tougher rules as it grapples with high-profile hacking incidents and rogue behavior by its models.

title: Arms-maker urges Europe to let defense firms take down hostile drones
content:
PARIS — Governments should change laws to allow defense companies to take down suspicious drones overflying their plants, said a senior executive at Franco-German arms-maker KNDS.

The call, which KNDS plans to take to Brussels, comes amid a wave of fires, sabotage attempts and espionage cases targeting European weapons manufacturers — several of which capitals have linked to Russia.

“It would be good if national legislation allowed defense companies to protect themselves against drones — especially first-person-view drones that pass through layered air defense,” KNDS Executive Vice President for International Development Marcel Grisnigt said in an interview.

Currently, “the only thing we can do is warn local authorities and ask them to take measures. Most of the time, it’s too late obviously, and the harm has already been done,” he added. “We are developing and producing countermeasures ourselves. They could be deployed to protect our own sites, but then you need to have the legal authorization.”
snippet: PARIS — Governments should change laws to allow defense companies to take down suspicious drones overflying their plants, said a senior executive at Franco-German arms-maker KNDS.
creator: Laura Kayali

title: Inside Zuckerberg, Huang’s push for White House AI pact
content:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg was the chief architect of the “morally binding” AI accords that emerged from Tuesday’s White House lunch with President Donald Trump, Speaker Mike Johnson and more than a dozen tech executives, according to five people familiar with the private meeting.

Zuckerberg, with the help of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, pitched the so-called AI accords to senior White House officials and some of the biggest names in tech during the luncheon, three of the people said. Both Huang as well as Trump administration officials helped shape the pact ahead of the meeting, according to two of the people.

All five people were granted anonymity because they were not authorized to share details of the discussions.

As part of the voluntary agreement, signatories would commit to the importance of enacting safeguards to mitigate potential risks from advanced AI models, but without a clear enforcement mechanism, it is unclear what if any consequences they may face for failing to do so.

title: ‘Absolute s–t’: EU’s Microsoft Teams alternative draws bad reviews from officials
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission has rolled out an alternative to Microsoft Teams — but officials using it aren’t impressed, with one describing the tool as “absolute shit.”

The Commission introduced Element Pro over the summer as a “sovereign back-up to Teams,” according to an internal staff memo seen by POLITICO. The platform is intended to provide a fallback for Commission communications if U.S.-based Teams becomes unavailable.

While Teams remains the Commission’s main communications tool, Element Pro is an “internal back-up … that helps ensure our business continuity” in the event of a “disruption,” the memo says.

But three officials have questioned why the Commission needs the new system — and whether it works well enough to serve as a genuine backup.

“I don’t understand the added value here,” one official wrote on an internal staff message board, seen by POLITICO. Another described the tool as “absolute shit.”

A third official said that, judging matters on how well Element Pro works compared to Teams, the U.S. would “instantly win the war” if it ever decided to switch off its technology. All the officials were granted anonymity to speak freely.
snippet: BRUSSELS — The European Commission has rolled out an alternative to Microsoft Teams — but officials using it aren’t impressed, with one describing the tool as “absolute shit.”
creator: Sebastian Starcevic

title: EU and Canada to announce sweeping new partnership pact
content:
BRUSSELS — The EU and Canada will use a landmark summit next month to announce an expansive new partnership, ranging from breaking down digital trade barriers to joint support for Ukraine and investing in fighting wildfires.

“The world is rapidly changing with unprecedented geopolitical challenges as well as challenges across trade, energy, technology, climate, and resources,” reads a draft joint statement to be issued by the two sides, circulated to EU ambassadors in preparation for the planned summit that begins on Oct. 29, and obtained by POLITICO.

The EU and Canada have been seeking to shore up their strategic ties as they grapple with the fallout from U.S. President Donald Trump’s trade war. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen this month proposed inviting Canada to become an associate member of the EU, triggering an immediate threat by Trump to impose tariffs.

“Canada and the EU, with our unparalleled trade access, shared values, and complementary economic strengths, can build a deeper and more integrated relationship,” the draft paper says.

title: EU accused of hiding environmental impact of data centers
content:
The European Union has shielded data centers from public scrutiny about how much energy they use, according to a formal complaint filed Monday against the European Commission.

The complaint lodged this week by Lighthouse Reports, and first reported by POLITICO, accuses the EU executive of setting up rules keeping the public from seeing how much energy and water are used by individual data centers.

This comes as public opposition to power-hungry AI data centers grows across Europe, while energy prices rise.

Lighthouse Reports, a Netherlands-based non-profit conducting cross-border investigations of alleged government and corporate wrongdoing, accuses the Commission of building a “wall of silence” about energy consumption.

EU policymakers are determined “to deny or deter access to, and obfuscate understanding of, how data centers are performing,” reads the complaint filed under the Aarhus Convention, a legally binding international treaty that gives the public rights to information and participation in environmental decision-making.
snippet: The European Union has shielded data centers from public scrutiny about how much energy they use, according to a formal complaint filed Monday against the European Commission.
creator: Mathieu Pollet

title: Andy Burnham keeps his options open on Brexit
content:
LIVERPOOL, England — Andy Burnham pledged to undertake the most ambitious review of Brexit since Britain left the EU.

But for now at least, he’s keeping all his options open.

Speaking at his party’s annual conference in Liverpool on Tuesday, the U.K. prime minister said the current plans to improve the Brexit settlement struck by the last Conservative government were “not enough” and that leaving the bloc had done “more harm than good.”

But Burnham didn’t pledge an immediate fix.

Instead, the newly-installed British PM said he would lay out “what I believe the different options are for Britain’s long-term relationship with our European partners” at a U.K.-EU summit later this year.

“And there are different options,” he said. “I will see if we can find consensus around one, which will give us clarity about our position and the future of the continent that we live in.”
